--- title: cacheComponents description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js. related: links: - app/getting-started/caching - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote --- Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route. ## Usage To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file, together with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching): ```ts filename="next.config.ts" import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` Set `partialPrefetching` explicitly. Leaving it unset logs a warning, because the first release of Cache Components did not include Partial Prefetching. Set it to `false` only while [migrating an app that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed. > **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge). When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations: - The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache` - The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) > **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components). Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed. Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together. > **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating. ## Navigation with Activity When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation. Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means: - Component state is preserved when navigating between routes - When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact - Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes. > **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth. Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing. ## Version History | Version | Change | | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 16.0.0 | `cacheComponents` stabilized and moved from `experimental.cacheComponents` to the top-level `cacheComponents` option. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. | --- title: partialPrefetching description: Configure the default link prefetch behavior to fetch only the static parts of each route. related: title: Related description: View related API references and guides. links: - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch - app/api-reference/components/link - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching --- `partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more. ## Usage ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` ```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher module.exports = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } ``` `partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation. ## Reference | Value | Description | | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `true` | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app. | | `false` | Keeps the previous prefetch behavior, for apps that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching was available. | Leaving the option unset behaves like `false` and logs a warning when `cacheComponents` is enabled. Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed. ## How prefetches resolve Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport. With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch. The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it. > **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client. A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching). > **Good to know**: If you use `` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail. ## Per-segment overrides A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route. ## Version History | Version | Change | | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 16.3.0 | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. | --- title: Dynamic Route Segments nav_title: Dynamic Segments description: Use Dynamic Segments to read URL path params and generate routes from dynamic data. related: title: Next Steps description: For more information on what to do next, we recommend the following sections links: - app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params --- A URL path is a sequence of path segments. In the App Router, a segment may be **static** (a literal value matched exactly) or **dynamic** (a placeholder that captures a value from the URL). When you don't know a segment's value ahead of time, define a Dynamic Segment to create routes from dynamic data. Next.js passes the captured values to your page via the path `params` prop, either filled in at request time or prerendered at build time. > **Good to know**: Dynamic Segments are often referred to as path params, route params, or URL params. ## Convention A Dynamic Segment can be created by wrapping a folder's name in square brackets: `[folderName]`. For example, a blog could include the following route `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` where `[slug]` is the Dynamic Segment for blog posts. ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher export default async function Page({ params, }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { const { slug } = await params return
My Post: {slug}
} ``` ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher export default async function Page({ params }) { const { slug } = await params return
My Post: {slug}
} ``` Dynamic Segments are passed as the `params` prop to [`layout`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [`page`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [`route`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), and [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#generatemetadata-function) functions. | Route | Example URL | `params` | | ------------------------- | ----------- | --------------- | | `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` | `/blog/a` | `{ slug: 'a' }` | | `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` | `/blog/b` | `{ slug: 'b' }` | | `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` | `/blog/c` | `{ slug: 'c' }` | Dynamic segments that appear before the [root layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout) are **root parameters**, which can additionally be read from any Server Component with [`next/root-params`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params). ### In Client Components In a Client Component **page**, dynamic segments from props can be accessed using the [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) API. ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 'use client' import { use } from 'react' export default function BlogPostPage({ params, }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { const { slug } = use(params) return (

{slug}

) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 'use client' import { use } from 'react' export default function BlogPostPage({ params }) { const { slug } = use(params) return (

{slug}

) } ``` Alternatively Client Components can use the [`useParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-params) hook to access the `params` anywhere in the Client Component tree. ### Catch-all Segments Dynamic Segments can be extended to **catch-all** subsequent segments by adding an ellipsis inside the brackets `[...folderName]`. For example, `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js` will match `/shop/clothes`, but also `/shop/clothes/tops`, `/shop/clothes/tops/t-shirts`, and so on. | Route | Example URL | `params` | | ---------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------- | | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js` | `/shop/a` | `{ slug: ['a'] }` | | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js` | `/shop/a/b` | `{ slug: ['a', 'b'] }` | | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js` | `/shop/a/b/c` | `{ slug: ['a', 'b', 'c'] }` | ### Optional Catch-all Segments Catch-all Segments can be made **optional** by including the parameter in double square brackets: `[[...folderName]]`. For example, `app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js` will **also** match `/shop`, in addition to `/shop/clothes`, `/shop/clothes/tops`, `/shop/clothes/tops/t-shirts`. The difference between **catch-all** and **optional catch-all** segments is that with optional, the route without the parameter is also matched (`/shop` in the example above). | Route | Example URL | `params` | | ------------------------------ | ------------- | --------------------------- | | `app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js` | `/shop` | `{ slug: undefined }` | | `app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js` | `/shop/a` | `{ slug: ['a'] }` | | `app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js` | `/shop/a/b` | `{ slug: ['a', 'b'] }` | | `app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js` | `/shop/a/b/c` | `{ slug: ['a', 'b', 'c'] }` | ### TypeScript When using TypeScript, you can add types for `params` depending on your configured route segment — use [`PageProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper), [`LayoutProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper), or [`RouteContext<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper) to type `params` in `page`, `layout`, and `route` respectively. Route `params` values are typed as `string`, `string[]`, or `undefined` (for optional catch-all segments), because their values aren't known until runtime. Users can enter any URL into the address bar, and these broad types help ensure that your application code handles all these possible cases. | Route | `params` Type Definition | | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` | `{ slug: string }` | | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js` | `{ slug: string[] }` | | `app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js` | `{ slug?: string[] }` | | `app/[categoryId]/[itemId]/page.js` | `{ categoryId: string, itemId: string }` | If you're working on a route where `params` can only have a fixed number of valid values, such as a `[locale]` param with a known set of language codes, you can use runtime validation to handle any invalid params a user may enter, and let the rest of your application work with the narrower type from your known set. ```tsx filename="/app/[locale]/page.tsx" import { notFound } from 'next/navigation' import type { Locale } from '@i18n/types' import { isValidLocale } from '@i18n/utils' function assertValidLocale(value: string): asserts value is Locale { if (!isValidLocale(value)) notFound() } export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/[locale]'>) { const { locale } = await props.params // locale is typed as string assertValidLocale(locale) // locale is now typed as Locale } ``` ## Behavior - Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async`/`await` or React's use function to access the values. - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. ### With Cache Components When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic route segments, how you handle params depends on whether you use [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params). Without `generateStaticParams`, param values are unknown during prerendering, making params runtime data. You must wrap param access in `` boundaries to provide fallback UI. With `generateStaticParams`, you provide sample param values that can be used at build time. """Supabase access for the job queue: runs, steps, frictions and screenshots.

Needs SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY in the environment (worker/.env).
"""

import os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from supabase import AsyncClient, acreate_client

BUCKET = "screenshots"

_client: AsyncClient | None = None


async def client() -> AsyncClient:
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = await acreate_client(os.environ["SUPABASE_URL"], os.environ["SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"])
    return _client


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


async def enqueue_run(url: str, goal: str, source: str = "live") -> dict:
    response = await (await client()).table("runs").insert(
        {"url": url, "goal": goal, "source": source}
    ).execute()
    return response.data[0]


async def claim_run() -> dict | None:
    """Take the oldest queued run and mark it running, or return None if the queue is empty."""
    response = await (await client()).rpc("claim_run").execute()
    return response.data[0] if response.data else None


async def add_step(
    run_id: str,
    idx: int,
    tool: str,
    thought: str,
    input: dict,
    result: dict,
    url: str | None,
    screenshot_path: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    await (await client()).table("steps").insert({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "idx": idx,
        "tool": tool,
        "thought": thought,
        "input": input,
        "result": result,
        "url": url,
        "screenshot_path": screenshot_path,
    }).execute()


async def add_friction(
    run_id: str,
    step_idx: int | None,
    kind: str,
    severity: str | None,
    expected: str,
    happened: str,
) -> None:
    await (await client()).table("frictions").insert({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "step_idx": step_idx,
        "kind": kind,
        "severity": severity,
        "expected": expected,
        "happened": happened,
    }).execute()


async def finish_run(run_id: str, result: dict, agent_version: str, brain_model: str) -> None:
    await (await client()).table("runs").update({
        "status": "done",
        "outcome": result.get("outcome"),
        "reason": result.get("reason"),
        "result": result,
        "cost_usd": result.get("usage", {}).get("estimated_cost_usd", {}).get("total"),
        "agent_version": agent_version,
        "brain_model": brain_model,
        "finished_at": _now(),
    }).eq("id", run_id).execute()


async def fail_run(
    run_id: str,
    error: str,
    agent_version: str | None = None,
    brain_model: str | None = None,
    result: dict | None = None,
) -> None:
    update = {"status": "failed", "error": error[:2000], "finished_at": _now()}
    if agent_version:
        update["agent_version"] = agent_version
    if brain_model:
        update["brain_model"] = brain_model
    if result is not None:
        update.update({
            "outcome": result.get("outcome"),
            "reason": result.get("reason"),
            "result": result,
            "cost_usd": result.get("usage", {}).get("estimated_cost_usd", {}).get("total"),
        })
    await (await client()).table("runs").update(update).eq("id", run_id).execute()


async def fail_stale_runs(minutes: int = 15) -> list[dict]:
    """Mark runs that have been running for longer than `minutes` as failed."""
    cutoff = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=minutes)).isoformat()
    response = await (await client()).table("runs").update({
        "status": "failed",
        "error": f"Stale: still running after {minutes} minutes (worker stopped or crashed).",
        "finished_at": _now(),
    }).eq("status", "running").lt("started_at", cutoff).execute()
    return response.data


async def upload_screenshot(run_id: str, local_path: Path) -> str:
    """Upload a PNG to the public screenshots bucket and return its public URL."""
    storage_path = f"{run_id}/{local_path.name}"
    bucket = (await client()).storage.from_(BUCKET)
    await bucket.upload(
        storage_path,
        local_path.read_bytes(),
        {"content-type": "image/png", "x-upsert": "true"},
    )
    return await bucket.get_public_url(storage_path)


class RunRecorder:
    """Writes one run's steps, frictions and screenshots to Supabase as they happen."""

    def __init__(self, run_id: str):
        self.run_id = run_id

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"RunRecorder(run_id={self.run_id!r})"

    async def step(self, idx, tool, thought, input, result, url, screenshot: Path | None) -> None:
        screenshot_url = await upload_screenshot(self.run_id, screenshot) if screenshot else None
        await add_step(self.run_id, idx, tool, thought, input, result, url, screenshot_url)

    async def friction(self, step_idx, kind, severity, expected, happened) -> None:
        await add_friction(self.run_id, step_idx, kind, severity, expected, happened)

"""Screenshot pages at a phone viewport over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

Usage: python cdp_shot.py OUT_DIR WIDTH name=url [name=url ...]
Prints console errors and the first part of each page's visible text.
"""
import asyncio, base64, json, subprocess, sys, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import websockets

CHROME = r"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"
PORT = 9333


async def main(out_dir: Path, width: int, targets: list[str]) -> None:
    proc = subprocess.Popen([
        CHROME, "--headless=new", f"--remote-debugging-port={PORT}", "--disable-gpu", "--hide-scrollbars",
        f"--user-data-dir={out_dir / 'cdp-profile'}", "about:blank",
    ], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    try:
        for _ in range(50):
            try:
                pages = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/json"))
                break
            except OSError:
                time.sleep(0.2)
        ws_url = next(p["webSocketDebuggerUrl"] for p in pages if p["type"] == "page")
        async with websockets.connect(ws_url, max_size=50_000_000) as ws:
            counter = 0
            events: list[dict] = []

            async def call(method, **params):
                nonlocal counter
                counter += 1
                my_id = counter
                await ws.send(json.dumps({"id": my_id, "method": method, "params": params}))
                while True:
                    msg = json.loads(await ws.recv())
                    if msg.get("id") == my_id:
                        if "error" in msg:
                            raise RuntimeError(msg["error"])
                        return msg.get("result", {})
                    events.append(msg)

            await call("Page.enable")
            await call("Runtime.enable")
            await call("Log.enable")
            await call("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", width=width, height=844,
                       deviceScaleFactor=1, mobile=width < 600)
            for target in targets:
                name, url = target.split("=", 1)
                events.clear()
                await call("Page.navigate", url=url)
                await asyncio.sleep(5)
                await call("Runtime.evaluate", expression="1")  # drain pending events
                height = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                     expression="document.documentElement.scrollHeight"))["result"]["value"]
                scroll_w = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                       expression="document.documentElement.scrollWidth"))["result"]["value"]
                text = (await call("Runtime.evaluate", returnByValue=True,
                                   expression="document.body.innerText"))["result"]["value"]
                shot = await call("Page.captureScreenshot", format="png", captureBeyondViewport=True,
                                  clip={"x": 0, "y": 0, "width": width, "height": min(height, 6000), "scale": 1})
                (out_dir / f"{name}.png").write_bytes(base64.b64decode(shot["data"]))
                errors = [
                    e["params"].get("entry", e["params"]).get("text") or json.dumps(e["params"])[:300]
                    for e in events
                    if e.get("method") in ("Log.entryAdded", "Runtime.exceptionThrown")
                    or (e.get("method") == "Runtime.consoleAPICalled" and e["params"].get("type") == "error")
                ]
                print(f"== {name}: height {height}, scrollWidth {scroll_w} (viewport {width})")
                for err in errors:
                    print("   console:", str(err)[:300])
                print("   text:", " | ".join(line for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip())[:500])
    finally:
        proc.terminate()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main(Path(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3:]))

The web app is built and passes typecheck, lint and `next build`. Nothing has touched your real Supabase yet: I tested against a fake Supabase I ran locally, and the new SQL has not been run anywhere.

**What I tested:**
- **URL checks:** I sent real requests to the running app. All of these were rejected with a plain message:
  - ftp addresses
  - localhost
  - addresses with a port (`:8080`, `:3000`)
  - 192.168.x.x
  - the cloud metadata IP 169.254.169.254
  - `::ffff:127.0.0.1` and `2130706433` (both are 127.0.0.1)
  - URLs with a username and password
  - single-word hosts
  - a domain that doesn't exist
  - `localtest.me`, a public name that resolves to 127.0.0.1
- **Other API errors:** missing permission box, a goal over 500 characters, a bad request body, and an unknown run id (404).
- **Full flow against the fake:** a normal submit returns the new run's id; a full queue returns 503; the hourly limit returns 429 with Retry-After; an unknown run returns 404.
- **Run page at 390 px (phone width), in Chrome:** I loaded every state: queued, running, done, failed and not found.
  - The running page picked up new steps every 2 seconds and stopped polling when the run finished.
  - Nothing scrolls sideways.
  - The report looked right in a screenshot; I tidied the wording on the agent-issue card after looking at it.
- **Key safety:** the browser bundle contains no key, no Supabase client code and no env variable names.

**Not tested:**
- The SQL itself.
- A real run going from the web app to the worker and back.
- The landing form's inline error messages in a browser (I tested the API behind them).
- Light mode: my screenshots rendered in dark mode.

**Choices you should know about:**
- **Queue limit:** a new run is rejected once 20 are already queued, so the queue never holds more than 20.
- **No race between limits:** one SQL function, `enqueue_web_run`, checks both limits and inserts the run in a single transaction, so two requests can't both slip past a limit.
- **Hashed IP:** the hash is keyed with the service role key unless you set `IP_HASH_SECRET`. The raw IP is never stored.
- **The rate limit isn't strong:** it trusts the `X-Forwarded-For` header, which is only safe behind a proxy that sets it (Vercel does). Locally anyone can fake it.
- **URL checks can be bypassed:** I check DNS when the form is submitted, but the worker's browser looks the name up again later and can follow redirects. A determined attacker could still reach a private address. Closing that properly means blocking private IPs inside the worker's browser.
- **Failed runs hide the reason:** the API returns a null reason for failed runs, because it's an internal error message. The page says "this tells you nothing about your site".
- **Report pages are marked noindex**, so search engines won't list them.
- **Packages:** I pinned `@supabase/supabase-js` to 2.117.2, the newest release that's at least two weeks old, plus `server-only`, which makes the build fail if the Supabase helper is ever imported into browser code. `npm install` reported audit warnings that I didn't investigate.

## What SQL to run

In the Supabase dashboard, open **SQL Editor → New query**, paste the whole of `supabase/schema.sql`, and click **Run**. It's safe to re-run, so it doesn't matter whether you already ran the earlier version. The new part is at the bottom: it adds an `ip_hash` column, an index on it, and the `enqueue_web_run` function, which only the service role can call.

To check it worked:
```sql
select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name = 'runs' and column_name = 'ip_hash';  -- 1 row
select proname from pg_proc where proname = 'enqueue_web_run';                                              -- 1 row
```

## How to run it locally

1. **`web/.env.local`:** add the same two values you put in `worker/.env`:
   ```
   SUPABASE_URL=https://<your-project-ref>.supabase.co
   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<service_role key>
   ```
   You can also add `IP_HASH_SECRET=<any long random string>`, which is optional. Never add a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` copy of the key.
2. **Terminal 1, the web app:**
   ```
   cd web
   npm install
   npm run dev
   ```
   Then open http://localhost:3000.
3. **Terminal 2, the worker:** from `worker/`, run `.venv\Scripts\python.exe main.py`. Without it, runs stay "Waiting for a free browser".
4. **Try it:** submit `https://www.saucedemo.com` with the permission box ticked. You'll land on `/run/<id>` and watch the steps arrive. You can't test your own `localhost` app this way, because the URL checks reject it.

New files are `web/lib/`, `web/app/api/runs/route.ts`, `web/app/api/runs/[id]/route.ts`, `web/app/run-form.tsx` and `web/app/run/[id]/`. I also changed `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx`, `globals.css`, `package.json` and `schema.sql`. Nothing is committed. If you want it, I can also add this session to `hackathon.md`.

An automated security review flagged the same gap I mentioned in my last message: the app checks the address only once, when the form is submitted.

- **The risk:** later, the worker's browser looks the site up again and follows redirects. A site could then send it to a private address, such as localhost or the cloud metadata service. On your laptop, that means your own machine and home network.
- **The fix:** block private addresses where the browser actually connects. The worker would check every request and navigation and reject private ones, or the worker would run behind a network proxy or firewall that blocks them. Either covers redirects.
- **When it matters:** before the web app is open to strangers. For local testing with sites you choose, the current check is enough.

I haven't changed anything, because the fix belongs in `worker/` and is outside what you asked for here. Want me to add the per-request blocking to the worker next?

async def _launch_local_browser(options: _LocalBrowserOptions) -> ResolvedBrowserSource:
    _validate_local_browser_options(options)
    chrome_path = _find_chrome_path(options.executable_path)
    port = _resolve_chrome_port(options.port)
    profile = _resolve_chrome_profile(options)
    flags = _local_browser_flags(
        options,
        port=port,
        user_data_dir=profile.path,
        disable_sandbox=_should_disable_chromium_sandbox(options),
    )
    process: _ChromeProcess | None = None
    try:
        try:
            launched_process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                chrome_path,
                *flags,
                stdin=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL,
                start_new_session=sys.platform != "win32",
            )
            process = launched_process
        except OSError as error:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to start Chrome: {error}") from error
        await _wait_for_chrome(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", launched_process)
    except BaseException as launch_error:
        try:
            if process is not None:
                await _close_local_chrome(process, profile)
            elif profile.remove:
                await _remove_chrome_profile(profile.path)
        except BaseException as cleanup_error:
            raise _combined_error(
                "Chrome launch failed and browser cleanup also failed",
                [launch_error, cleanup_error],
            ) from launch_error
        raise

    async def close() -> None:
        await _close_local_chrome(launched_process, profile)

    return ResolvedBrowserSource(

        keep_alive=options.keep_alive or False,
        _close_callback=close,
    )

    if options.viewport is not None and (

    if options.device_scale_factor is not None and (

            raise ValueError("Chrome proxy server is required")

    options: _LocalBrowserOptions,
    *,
    port: int,
    user_data_dir: Path,
    disable_sandbox: bool,
) -> list[str]:
    ignored_default_args = options.ignore_default_args
    ignored_flags = set(ignored_default_args) if isinstance(ignored_default_args, list) else set()
    include_defaults = ignored_default_args is not True
    viewport = (
        options.viewport if options.viewport is not None else LocalViewport(width=1280, height=800)
    )
    window_size_flag = f"--window-size={viewport.width},{viewport.height}"

    return [
        *(
            [flag for flag in _DEFAULT_CHROME_FLAGS if flag not in ignored_flags]
            if include_defaults
            else []
        ),
        *(

import os

from stagehand import Stagehand, local_browser

from config import DEVICE_SCALE_FACTOR, LOOKUP_MODEL
from egress import CHROME_EXTRA_ARGS, CHROME_PROXY_BYPASS, EgressGuard


async def open_browser():
    """Start the egress guard, launch a local Chrome window behind it and attach Stagehand.

    Every request Chrome makes goes through the guard, which refuses private,
    loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses (see egress.py).
    """
    guard = EgressGuard()
    await guard.start()
    try:
        browser = await local_browser.launch(
            headless=False,
            device_scale_factor=DEVICE_SCALE_FACTOR,
            proxy_server=guard.proxy_server,
            proxy_bypass=CHROME_PROXY_BYPASS,
            args=CHROME_EXTRA_ARGS,
        )
    except BaseException:
        await guard.close()
        raise
    try:
        stagehand = await Stagehand.create(
            browser=browser,
            model=LOOKUP_MODEL,
            model_api_key=os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"],
        )
    except BaseException:
        try:
            await browser.close()
        finally:
            await guard.close()
        raise
    page = (await browser.context.pages())[0]
    return browser, stagehand, page, guard


async def close_browser(browser, stagehand, guard):
    """Close Stagehand before the browser, as the Stagehand docs require, then the guard."""
    try:
        await stagehand.close()
    finally:
        try:
            await browser.close()
        finally:
            await guard.close()

"""Tests for the egress guard.

Usage: python -m unittest test_egress -v

The redirect test opens a real Chrome window and goes through first_visit, but
stops before the first model call, so it costs nothing. It needs
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in worker/.env only because Stagehand.create requires one.
Test servers listen on loopback, so 127.0.0.1 is treated as public for the
test origin; the redirect target 127.0.0.2 stays private.
"""

import asyncio
import ipaddress
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv(Path(__file__).parent / ".env")

import egress  # noqa: E402

REAL_IS_BLOCKED = egress.is_blocked_address
TEST_ORIGIN = ipaddress.ip_address("127.0.0.1")


def origin_is_public(address):
    return False if address == TEST_ORIGIN else REAL_IS_BLOCKED(address)


class Server:
    """A tiny HTTP server that counts requests and answers with a fixed response."""

    def __init__(self, host: str, response: bytes):
        self.host, self.response, self.hits, self.port = host, response, 0, 0

    async def __aenter__(self):
        async def handle(reader, writer):
            await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
            self.hits += 1
            writer.write(self.response)
            await writer.drain()
            writer.close()

        self.server = await asyncio.start_server(handle, self.host, 0)
        self.port = self.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.close()
        await self.server.wait_closed()


def http_response(status: str, headers: str = "", body: str = "") -> bytes:
    return (f"HTTP/1.1 {status}\r\n{headers}Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{body}").encode()


async def proxy_request(guard: egress.EgressGuard, request: str) -> str:
    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", guard.port)
    writer.write(request.encode())
    await writer.drain()
    status = (await reader.readline()).decode().strip()
    writer.close()
    return status


class AddressRules(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_non_public_addresses_are_blocked(self):
        for address in ["127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.5", "172.16.3.4", "192.168.1.1", "169.254.169.254", "100.64.0.1",
                        "0.0.0.0", "::1", "fd00::1", "fe80::1", "::ffff:127.0.0.1", "64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe"]:
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                self.assertTrue(egress.is_blocked_address(ipaddress.ip_address(address)))

    def test_public_addresses_are_allowed(self):
        for address in ["8.8.8.8", "93.184.215.14", "2606:4700:4700::1111"]:
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                self.assertFalse(egress.is_blocked_address(ipaddress.ip_address(address)))


class ProxyRefusals(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_private_targets_are_refused_and_never_contacted(self):
        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:
            guard = egress.EgressGuard()
            await guard.start()
            try:
                plain = await proxy_request(
                    guard, f"GET http://127.0.0.2:{secret.port}/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.2\r\n\r\n")
                tunnel = await proxy_request(guard, "CONNECT localhost:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost:443\r\n\r\n")
                metadata = await proxy_request(
                    guard, "GET http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 169.254.169.254\r\n\r\n")
            finally:
                await guard.close()
        self.assertIn("403", plain)
        self.assertIn("403", tunnel)
        self.assertIn("403", metadata)
        self.assertEqual(secret.hits, 0)
        self.assertEqual([b["host"] for b in guard.blocks], ["127.0.0.2", "localhost", "169.254.169.254"])

    async def test_unresolvable_host_is_not_a_safety_block(self):
        guard = egress.EgressGuard()
        await guard.start()
        try:
            status = await proxy_request(
                guard, "GET http://no-such-host.invalid/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: no-such-host.invalid\r\n\r\n")
        finally:
            await guard.close()
        self.assertIn("502", status)
        self.assertEqual(guard.blocks, [])


class RedirectInRealBrowser(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_redirect_to_private_address_is_refused_and_ends_run_as_blocked(self):
        from visit import first_visit

        async with Server("127.0.0.2", http_response("200 OK", body="secret")) as secret:
            redirect = http_response("302 Found", f"Location: http://127.0.0.2:{secret.port}/secret\r\n")
            async with Server("127.0.0.1", redirect) as origin:
                with mock.patch("egress.is_blocked_address", origin_is_public):
                    result = await first_visit(
                        f"http://127.0.0.1:{origin.port}/", "Look around.", "test-egress-redirect")

        self.assertGreaterEqual(origin.hits, 1, "the allowed origin should have been reached through the proxy")
        self.assertEqual(secret.hits, 0, "the private redirect target must never be contacted")
        self.assertEqual(result["outcome"], "blocked")
        self.assertIn("127.0.0.2", result["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(result["steps"], 0, "the run should end before any model call")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

    async def _devtools_tunnel(self, reader, writer, host: str, port: int) -> None:
        """Forward a tunnel to Chrome's DevTools port only if its first request comes from an extension.

        Stagehand launches Chrome with --remote-allow-origins=*, so DevTools itself
        would accept a websocket from any page. A DevTools websocket is plain HTTP
        inside the tunnel, and browsers always send an Origin header that pages
        cannot forge, so the guard checks it here instead.
        """
        writer.write(b"HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established\r\n\r\n")
        await writer.drain()
        try:
            head = await asyncio.wait_for(reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n"), HEADER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
        except (asyncio.IncompleteReadError, asyncio.LimitOverrunError, asyncio.TimeoutError):
            return
        request_line, *header_lines = head.decode("latin-1").split("\r\n")
        origin = next(
            (line.split(":", 1)[1].strip() for line in header_lines if line.lower().startswith("origin:")), ""
        )
        task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(
            _guarded_devtools_check(origin, request_line[:200]), context=self._context.copy()
        )
        if not (await task)["allowed"]:
            self.blocks.append({"host": host, "port": port, "url": f"DevTools: {request_line[:200]}",
                                "addresses": [host], "reason": f"DevTools request from origin {origin or 'none'}"})
            return
        upstream_reader, upstream = await _open_vetted(["127.0.0.1"], port)
        if upstream is None:
            return
        try:
            upstream.write(head)
            await asyncio.gather(_pipe(reader, upstream), _pipe(upstream_reader, writer))
        finally:
            upstream.close()


@neatlogs.span(kind="GUARDRAIL", name="devtools_check")
async def _guarded_devtools_check(origin: str, request_line: str) -> dict:
    """Allow a tunnel to the browser's DevTools port only for a browser extension (Stagehand's)."""
    allowed = origin.startswith("chrome-extension://")
    return {"allowed": allowed, "origin": origin or None, "request": request_line}

### 2026-10-10 — Supabase job queue (committed as `6a08b29`)

Not logged at the time, so this entry is recorded afterwards.

Completed:
- `supabase/schema.sql`: `runs`, `steps` and `frictions` tables (RLS on, no policies, granted to `service_role` only), a `claim_run()` function using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, and a public `screenshots` bucket.
- `worker/db.py` (enqueue, claim, steps, frictions, finish/fail, stale-run sweep, screenshot upload) and a `RunRecorder` that writes each step, friction and screenshot as it happens. `run_once.py` still works without a database.
- `worker/main.py`: a worker loop that claims one run at a time inside `neatlogs.identify(session_id="run_<id>")`. It marks runs still running after 15 minutes as failed, and on the first Ctrl+C it finishes the current run before flushing neatlogs once. `worker/enqueue.py` queues a run from the command line.
- The builder committed this as `6a08b29` (2026-10-10 16:36 IST) with the trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M4JQVWZEF4R78NT2M170VMW8`.

Tests that ran:
- The worker loop against an in-memory fake of `db.py`, with Ctrl+Break sent at step 2. The run finished (`achieved`, 9 steps, $0.0248) and every step reached the recorder. The worker then stopped without claiming another run, shut neatlogs down once, and exited 0.
- `run_once.py` with no database: `achieved` in 9 steps, $0.0243.

Not yet verified:
- Anything against a real Supabase project (schema, RPC, inserts, storage uploads).

### 2026-10-10 — Web app

Completed:
- `web/` is now the product front end. It reads `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from `web/.env.local` on the server only. The client module imports `server-only`, so the build fails if browser code ever imports it.
- Landing page (`/`): the one-line promise, a URL field, an optional goal, a required "This is my app or I have permission to test it" checkbox, and a plain note that we click around like a visitor, may create a test account, and never enter payment details.
- `POST /api/runs` validates the URL. It accepts only http(s) on the default port with no credentials. It rejects localhost and `.local`/`.internal`-style names, private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and other reserved IPv4/IPv6 ranges (including IPv4-mapped and NAT64 forms), and hosts that resolve to any of them. An empty goal gets a default goal.
- Limits are enforced in one SQL function, `enqueue_web_run`, under an advisory lock so concurrent requests cannot race past them: at most 20 queued runs, and 5 runs per visitor per hour. Visitors are identified by an HMAC of the IP, stored as the new `runs.ip_hash` column; the raw IP is never stored.
- `GET /api/runs/[id]` returns the run, steps and frictions, without the IP hash or the raw worker error.
- `/run/[id]` polls every 2 seconds until the run is done or failed. While running it shows the status and each step as it arrives (thought, action, result, screenshot). When finished it shows a report: the outcome and reason, frictions split into "Problems with the site" and "Our agent's own issues", the step timeline, time, cost, a copy-link button, and the line "This is a simulated user. Treat findings as leads to check."
- Unhappy states each have their own message: invalid URL, queue full (503), rate limited (429 with Retry-After), run failed, run not found.

Tests that ran:
- `tsc`, ESLint and `next build` passed. A scan of the built browser bundle found no key, no Supabase client code and no server env variable names.
- 14 requests against the running app returned the expected rejection, among them localhost, `:8080`, 192.168.x.x, 169.254.169.254, `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, `2130706433`, a nonexistent domain, and `localtest.me` (a public name that resolves to 127.0.0.1).
- Against a local fake of Supabase's REST API: a normal enqueue (201), queue full (503), rate limited (429), and done, failed, queued and missing runs.
- Every run-page state rendered in Chrome at 390 px with no horizontal scroll. The running page picked up new steps and stopped polling when the run finished.

Not yet verified:
- `schema.sql` and the end-to-end flow (web → queue → worker → report) on a real Supabase project.
- Light mode, and the landing form's inline errors in a real browser.

Security note: an automated review flagged that the URL is checked only at submission. The worker's browser resolves names again and follows redirects, so it could still be steered to a private address. Fixed in the next entry.

### 2026-10-10 — Egress guard in the worker

Completed:
- `worker/egress.py`: a local proxy that every request from Chrome must go through. Chrome launches with `--proxy-server` pointing at it, `<-loopback>` to remove Chrome's built-in localhost bypass, and WebRTC limited to proxied connections.
- For each new host the guard resolves the name itself, refuses it if any address is not public, and then connects only to an address it checked. Not public means private, loopback, link-local (including the 169.254.169.254 metadata address), CGNAT, unique-local, multicast or reserved, with IPv4-mapped and NAT64 forms unwrapped. Connecting to the checked address, rather than resolving again, stops DNS rebinding. Because the check happens per connection, redirects, subresources and websockets are all covered.
- Each check runs in a neatlogs `GUARDRAIL` span (`egress_check`), once per host per run.
- A refused request ends the run as `blocked`, with a reason naming the host and address. The check runs before every model call and once more after the loop. A host that simply does not resolve is refused quietly and does not end the run.
- Stagehand's built-in extension connects from inside Chrome to Chrome's own DevTools port, so that tunnel is allowed, but only when its first request carries a `chrome-extension://` Origin. Pages cannot forge that header. The check runs in a `GUARDRAIL` span (`devtools_check`). This also closes a gap that existed before: Stagehand launches Chrome with `--remote-allow-origins=*`, so a page could previously have connected to DevTools.

Tests that ran (`python -m unittest test_egress`, 6 tests, all pass):
- Address rules for blocked and allowed addresses.
- Through the proxy, plain HTTP to 127.0.0.2, a tunnel to `localhost`, and the metadata IP all got 403, and the private test server received 0 requests.
- The DevTools port refused a page Origin and accepted an extension Origin.
- An unresolvable host got 502 and did not count as a safety block.
- Redirect test in a real Chrome window through `first_visit`: a public-looking origin returned a 302 to `127.0.0.2`. The private server received 0 requests, and the run ended `blocked` with 0 steps (no model call).
- Negative control: with Chrome's loopback bypass left on, the same redirect test fails (the private server got 2 requests), so the test depends on the guard.
- A real visit to saucedemo through the guard (Haiku brain): `achieved` in 9 steps, $0.0292, no requests refused.

Failure found and fixed during the session:
- The first real run failed with "CDP websocket failed to open". Once loopback went through the guard, Stagehand's extension could not reach Chrome's DevTools port. The fix is the extension-only DevTools rule above.

Not yet verified:
- Whether the `egress_check` and `devtools_check` spans nest under the run in the neatlogs dashboard. The guard copies the run's context when it starts so they should.

The worker now refuses any browser request or navigation to private, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses, including after redirects. When that happens the run ends as `blocked`. All 6 tests in `worker/test_egress.py` pass, and a real saucedemo run through the guard reached the goal in 9 steps for $0.0292.

**How it works:**
- **One route out:** the worker starts a small filtering proxy (`worker/egress.py`) and launches Chrome so every request goes through it, including localhost. Chrome normally lets localhost skip a proxy; that exception is turned off. Redirects, images, scripts and websockets are all covered.
- **Check, then pin:** for each new host, the proxy looks up the name itself, refuses it if any address isn't public, and connects only to the address it checked. A site can't swap in a private address after the check.
- **neatlogs:** each check runs in a `GUARDRAIL` span named `egress_check`, once per host per run.
- **Ending the run:** the agent loop checks for a refusal before every model call and once after the loop. It ends the run as `blocked` with a reason like: "Stopped for safety: the site sent the browser to 127.0.0.2, which is a private, local or cloud-metadata address…". The web report shows it as "Got blocked" with that text.
- **Dead domains:** a host that doesn't exist (a dead analytics domain, say) is just refused. It doesn't end the run.

**Something you should know:** my first real run failed with "CDP websocket failed to open".
- **Cause:** Stagehand puts its own extension inside Chrome, and that extension connects to Chrome's local debugging port. The guard was refusing it.
- **Bigger issue:** Stagehand launches Chrome with a setting (`--remote-allow-origins=*`) that lets any page connect to that debugging port. A web page could have taken over the browser, and that was true before today's change too.
- **Fix:** the guard now lets connections reach that port only when they come from a browser extension. Pages can't fake this. The check runs in its own `GUARDRAIL` span (`devtools_check`). This closes both problems.

**The tests:**
- **Address rules:** blocked versus allowed addresses.
- **Private targets:** private IPs, `localhost` and the metadata IP all got 403 through the proxy, and the private test server received nothing.
- **Debugging port:** opens for an extension, refused for a page.
- **Dead domains:** refused without ending the run.
- **Redirect, in a real Chrome window, through `first_visit`:** a test site returned a redirect to 127.0.0.2. The server on 127.0.0.2 received 0 requests, and the run ended `blocked` with 0 steps, so there was no model cost. This is the test you asked for.
- **Control:** with Chrome's normal localhost exception left on, the same redirect test fails (the private server got 2 requests). So the test really depends on the guard.

**Trade-offs:**
- **Strict:** any refused request ends the run, including a stray third-party file on a private address, like a leftover `localhost` dev script. That's what you asked for.
- **One layer only:** the guard runs inside the worker process. A firewall on the worker machine would be a second layer, and none is set up.
- **Not seen yet:** I haven't confirmed in the neatlogs dashboard that the new spans appear under the run.

"""Token and cost accounting for one run: the brain model plus Stagehand's lookup model."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from config import LOOKUP_MODEL, PRICES

CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER = 1.25
CACHE_READ_MULTIPLIER = 0.10


def _price(model: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    return PRICES.get(model.removeprefix("anthropic/"), (0.0, 0.0))


@dataclass
class RunUsage:
    model_input: int = 0
    model_cache_write: int = 0
    model_cache_read: int = 0
    model_output: int = 0
    model_cost: float = 0.0
    models_used: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    stagehand_prompt: int = 0
    stagehand_completion: int = 0
    stagehand_cached: int = 0

    def add_response(self, response) -> None:
        usage = response.usage
        cache_write = usage.cache_creation_input_tokens or 0
        cache_read = usage.cache_read_input_tokens or 0
        self.model_input += usage.input_tokens
        self.model_cache_write += cache_write
        self.model_cache_read += cache_read
        self.model_output += usage.output_tokens
        self.models_used.add(response.model)
        input_price, output_price = _price(response.model)
        self.model_cost += (
            usage.input_tokens * input_price
            + cache_write * input_price * CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER
            + cache_read * input_price * CACHE_READ_MULTIPLIER
            + usage.output_tokens * output_price
        ) / 1_000_000

    def set_stagehand(self, metrics) -> None:
        """Stagehand's metrics are cumulative for the session, so store the latest snapshot."""
        self.stagehand_prompt = int(metrics.total_prompt_tokens)
        self.stagehand_completion = int(metrics.total_completion_tokens)
        self.stagehand_cached = int(metrics.total_cached_input_tokens)

    @property
    def stagehand_cost(self) -> float:
        return stagehand_cost(self.stagehand_prompt, self.stagehand_completion, self.stagehand_cached)

    @property
    def total_tokens(self) -> int:
        return (
            self.model_input + self.model_cache_write + self.model_cache_read + self.model_output
            + self.stagehand_prompt + self.stagehand_completion
        )

    @property
    def total_cost(self) -> float:
        return self.model_cost + self.stagehand_cost

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "brain_models": sorted(self.models_used),
            "model_tokens": {
                "input": self.model_input,
                "cache_write": self.model_cache_write,
                "cache_read": self.model_cache_read,
                "output": self.model_output,
            },
            "stagehand_tokens": {
                "model": LOOKUP_MODEL,
                "prompt": self.stagehand_prompt,
                "completion": self.stagehand_completion,
                "cached_input": self.stagehand_cached,
            },
            "total_tokens": self.total_tokens,
            "estimated_cost_usd": {
                "model": round(self.model_cost, 5),
                "stagehand": round(self.stagehand_cost, 5),
                "total": round(self.total_cost, 5),
            },
        }


def stagehand_cost(prompt: int, completion: int, cached: int) -> float:
    input_price, output_price = _price(LOOKUP_MODEL)
    uncached = max(prompt - cached, 0)
    return (
        uncached * input_price + cached * input_price * CACHE_READ_MULTIPLIER + completion * output_price
    ) / 1_000_000
import os
import socket

from stagehand import Stagehand, local_browser

from config import DEVICE_SCALE_FACTOR, LOOKUP_MODEL
from egress import CHROME_EXTRA_ARGS, CHROME_PROXY_BYPASS, EgressGuard


async def open_browser():
    """Start the egress guard, launch a local Chrome window behind it and attach Stagehand.

    Every request Chrome makes goes through the guard, which refuses private,
    loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses (see egress.py).
    """
    guard = EgressGuard()
    await guard.start()
    guard.devtools_port = _free_port()
    try:
        browser = await local_browser.launch(
            headless=False,
            port=guard.devtools_port,
            device_scale_factor=DEVICE_SCALE_FACTOR,
            proxy_server=guard.proxy_server,
            proxy_bypass=CHROME_PROXY_BYPASS,
            args=CHROME_EXTRA_ARGS,
        )
    except BaseException:
        await guard.close()
        raise
    try:
        stagehand = await Stagehand.create(
            browser=browser,
            model=LOOKUP_MODEL,
            model_api_key=os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"],
        )
    except BaseException:
        try:
            await browser.close()
        finally:
            await guard.close()
        raise
    page = (await browser.context.pages())[0]
    return browser, stagehand, page, guard


def _free_port() -> int:
    with socket.socket() as probe:
        probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return probe.getsockname()[1]


async def close_browser(browser, stagehand, guard):
    """Close Stagehand before the browser, as the Stagehand docs require, then the guard."""
    try:
        await stagehand.close()
    finally:
        try:
            await browser.close()
        finally:
            await guard.close()

## Migrating to Claude Haiku 5.5

> **Model ID `claude-haiku-5-5` is authoritative as written here.** When the user asks to migrate to Claude Haiku 5.5, write `model="claude-haiku-5-5"` exactly (a fixed ID with no date suffix and no separate alias; `anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` on Amazon Bedrock). Do **not** WebFetch to verify - this guide is the source of truth for migration target IDs. The corresponding entry exists in `shared/models.md`.

Claude Haiku 5.5 succeeds Claude Haiku 4.5 as the Haiku-class model, for high-volume, latency-sensitive work such as classification, routing, extraction, and sub-agent tasks. 1M token context window and 128K max output, up from 200K and 64K. **Pricing has two rate cards, chosen by prompt length:** $0.10 / $0.50 per MTok input / output when the prompt is 100K tokens or fewer, and $0.50 / $2.50 when it is longer; cache reads are 0.1x the input rate, 5-minute cache writes 1.25x, and 1-hour cache writes 2x (Claude Haiku 4.5 is $1 / $5 at any prompt length). For a user who is budgeting on the figure, WebFetch the Pricing row in `shared/live-sources.md` first. Available on the Claude API (`claude-haiku-5-5`), Amazon Bedrock (`anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5`), Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry (all three as `claude-haiku-5-5`). The SDK constants listed below may be missing from the SDK version a project pins; the bare string `"claude-haiku-5-5"` works in every SDK (with the `anthropic.` prefix on Amazon Bedrock). Existing Claude Haiku 4.5 prompts should work well without changes; the model is substantially better at instruction following and at running as a sub-agent, across coding and knowledge work.

**Claude Haiku 5.5 is the default Haiku migration target.** This section covers code that calls Claude Haiku 4.5. A caller on Haiku 3 or 3.5 applies § Additional Changes When Coming from 3.x / 4.0 / 4.1 -> 4.6 first, then this section. To move a Haiku workload up to a Sonnet or Opus model instead, use that model's section (§ Migrating to Claude Sonnet 5.5 covers arrival from Claude Haiku 4.5). Claude Opus 5.5 stays the default model for new code; target Claude Haiku 5.5 when the user asks for Haiku or for a fast, low-cost model.

**What changes:** five breaking changes for code running on Claude Haiku 4.5 (manual thinking budgets 400 - thinking is adaptive only; non-default sampling parameters 400; assistant prefill 400; on the Claude API and Google Cloud the `computer_20250124` tool 400s - use the computer toolset; editing earlier turns invalidates replayed thinking blocks), four changes that fail no request (thinking is on by default, so a response can begin with `thinking` blocks; thinking text is omitted by default; the same text counts as about 30% more tokens; thinking blocks stay with the account that produced them), safety classifiers that can decline a request (new for code coming from Claude Haiku 4.5, with no server-side fallback - § Safeguards), and three additions (the `effort` parameter, the larger context window and output, and the browser use tool). § Behavioral shifts has the prompt changes worth testing.

### Breaking change 1: manual thinking budgets return a 400 - adaptive thinking only

Claude Haiku 4.5 supports only manual extended thinking with a token budget. On Claude Haiku 5.5, `thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N}` returns a 400. Send `{"type": "adaptive"}` (or omit `thinking`) and set how much the model thinks with `output_config.effort`. Where the budget was small to save tokens, choose a lower effort level.

```python
# Before - Claude Haiku 4.5
client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-4-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    thinking={"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 8000},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "..."}],
)

# After - Claude Haiku 5.5
client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    thinking={"type": "adaptive"},
    output_config={"effort": "medium"},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "..."}],
)
```

The per-language spelling is in **Per-SDK Syntax Reference** -> `thinking` above.

### Thinking is on by default - a response can begin with `thinking` blocks

Claude Haiku 4.5 thinks only when a request asks for it. Claude Haiku 5.5 runs adaptive thinking when the request doesn't set `thinking`, so code that never mentioned thinking now gets it. No request fails, but four things change:

- **Read content blocks by `type`, not by position.** A response can begin with one or more `thinking` blocks, so code that reads the first content block as the answer (`response.content[0].text`) breaks.
- **Thinking counts toward `max_tokens`.** A cap sized for a short answer - `max_tokens: 50` on a one-word classification - can be used up by thinking, and the response stops with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` after a `thinking` block and before any text. Raise the cap to leave room for thinking, or choose a lower effort level.
- **Thinking text is omitted by default.** Each `thinking` block comes back with an empty `thinking` field and only a `signature`, where Claude Haiku 4.5 returned summarized thinking. To receive summaries, set `thinking: {"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"}`. A serializer that skips empty blocks removes the thinking - keep the block even when its text is empty.
- **Pass `thinking` blocks back unmodified** with tool results.

**Use effort as the lever, not `disabled`.** Where Claude Haiku 4.5 ran without thinking, or with a small budget to save tokens, leave `thinking` unset (or `{"type": "adaptive"}`) and choose a lower effort level: the model thinks less, and it can skip thinking entirely on simpler requests.

```python
# A short-output route moved from Claude Haiku 4.5
client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-5-5",
    max_tokens=1024,  # room for thinking plus the one-word answer
    output_config={"effort": "low"},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Classify as positive/negative/neutral (one word): ..."}],
)
```

**Turning thinking off is still accepted, with limits.** `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` works at effort `low`, `medium`, and `high`; with `xhigh` or `max` it returns a 400 - lower the effort level, or set `thinking` to `{"type": "adaptive"}`. With thinking off, three more things hold: a per-message effort that differs from the level in effect returns a 400; `thinking.block_binding` returns a 400 (breaking change 5); and the model can skip a tool call it needs when the request also asks for JSON output (§ Behavioral shifts). `{"type": "between_tools"}` is accepted only by Claude Sonnet 5.5 and returns a 400 here.

**Forced tool calls skip thinking.** Claude Haiku 5.5 accepts a forced `tool_choice` (`any` or a named tool), with thinking on too, but the response then starts with the tool call and has no `thinking` block. To let the model think before it calls a tool, use `tool_choice: {"type": "auto"}` and say in the prompt when to use the tool.

### Breaking change 2: non-default sampling parameters return a 400

Claude Haiku 4.5 accepts `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k`. On Claude Haiku 5.5, omit all three and guide the model's behavior from the prompt instead. The accepted values are narrow: `temperature` must be `1`, and `top_p` must be `0.99`, its default; any other value of either returns a 400 (a `top_p` of `1` included), and so does any `top_k` value, and so does a request that sends both `temperature` and `top_p`. This holds on every request, whether or not thinking is used. `temperature=0` on a classification route is the common case: remove it, and constrain the output with structured outputs or an enum-valued tool. The per-language fields are in **Per-SDK Syntax Reference** -> Sampling parameters above.

### Breaking change 3: assistant prefill returns a 400

A prefill is a final assistant turn in `messages` that the model continues. Claude Haiku 4.5 accepts one when thinking is off. Claude Haiku 5.5 rejects it with a 400, with thinking turned off too. End `messages` with a user turn, and replace each prefill according to what it was for:

- **Output format:** structured outputs (`output_config.format`), or a tool with enum fields for classification. Where the caller's platform doesn't offer structured outputs for this model (`shared/platform-availability.md`), use tools.
- **Preambles:** ask in the system prompt for a direct answer.
- **Continuations:** move them to the user message, for example *"Your previous response was interrupted and ended with `[previous_response]`. Continue from where you left off."*
- **Context reminders:** put them in the user turn.

The per-language edit is in **Per-SDK Syntax Reference** -> Prefill replacement above.

### Breaking change 4: computer use needs the toolset on the Claude API and Google Cloud

Claude Haiku 4.5 supports computer use through the `computer_20250124` tool with the `computer-use-2025-01-24` beta header. On the Claude API and Google Cloud, Claude Haiku 5.5 supports computer use only through the `computer_toolset_20260801` toolset, and a request that declares `computer_20250124` returns a 400. To move an integration: drop the `computer-use-2025-01-24` beta header, replace the `tools` entry with `{"type": "computer_toolset_20260801"}`, and make the agent-loop changes - dispatch on each member `tool_use` block's `name` and `toolset_name` rather than on `input.action`, handle every such block in a turn, and echo `toolset_name` on results; zoom is on by default in the toolset, so if the environment doesn't implement it add `"configs": {"zoom": {"enabled": false}}` (`shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Computer Use; § Migrating to Claude Opus 5.5 -> Breaking change 4). If the request sends the `fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14` beta header, replace it with `eager_input_streaming: true` on each tool that needs it: alongside a toolset entry the header returns a 400. For Amazon Bedrock and the other platforms, WebFetch the computer use tool page's Compatibility section (`shared/live-sources.md`) before choosing a version - don't assume the Bedrock exception that Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 have carries over to this model.

On the Claude API and Google Cloud, Claude Haiku 5.5 also supports the browser use tool (`browser_toolset_20260801`) for tasks inside webpages; Claude Haiku 4.5 doesn't.

### The same text counts as about 30% more tokens

Claude Haiku 5.5 uses a newer tokenizer than Claude Haiku 4.5: the same input text produces approximately 30% more tokens, and the exact increase depends on the content. Requests, responses, and streaming events keep the same shape, and no code change is required. What changes is anything measured or budgeted in tokens:

- `usage` fields and `count_tokens` results are higher for the same text.
- A given number of tokens holds less text.
- A `max_tokens` limit tuned for Claude Haiku 4.5 may cut off equivalent output.
- The cost of an equivalent request changes in both directions - more tokens, at a different per-token rate, on whichever rate card the prompt length selects.

Count prompts with `model` set to `claude-haiku-5-5` rather than reusing counts measured on Claude Haiku 4.5, and re-baseline cost dashboards before reacting to a measured shift.

### Breaking change 5: editing earlier turns invalidates thinking blocks

A Claude Haiku 5.5 thinking block stays valid only while everything sent before it is unchanged: a request that sends a thinking block back after a change to `system`, `tools`, or earlier `messages` returns a 400. Claude Haiku 4.5 doesn't run this check. It is the history-editing check Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 run: enforced by default for accounts created on or after August 31, 2026, 00:00 UTC, and on older accounts only for requests that set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior`. Keep conversations append-only - the append-only replacements (mid-conversation `role: "system"` messages, which Claude Haiku 5.5 supports with no beta header; turn-scoped reminders; server-side compaction or context editing) and the three-step check are in § Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 from Claude Fable 5. As on Claude Sonnet 5.5, **`block_binding` works only with `thinking: {"type": "adaptive"}`**: with `{"type": "disabled"}`, keep the history append-only, or strip the thinking blocks from the edited turn on. With threshold compaction, thinking blocks from before a `compaction` block aren't carried forward; remove the `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` blocks from any assistant turn re-inserted after a compaction block (or set `drop_block`).

### Thinking blocks stay with the account that produced them

Thinking blocks from Claude Haiku 5.5 work only in the account that produced them, or in an account linked to it. When another account sends one of these blocks, the API drops the block before the model sees it, and the request succeeds without that reasoning. This matters only for code that stores conversations and replays them through a different account - for example a service that serves several customers from one conversation store. Replay each conversation through the account that produced it.

shared/cost-optimization.md:111:- **On models that run the preserved-thinking check, an edit to `system`, `tools`, or earlier messages breaks the model's earlier reasoning as well as the cache.** Each thinking block is tied to the conversation that produced it, and the edits that invalidate it are the same edits that restart the cache, so one discipline serves both: keep `system` and `tools` fixed for the session and treat `messages` as append-only. `cache_control` markers, `effort`, `max_tokens`, and `tool_choice` are outside the check. A diff that moves content out of `system` or `tools` is still an edit for conversations in flight when it deploys: have the diff keep sending the stored `system` and `tools` bytes to those conversations and the new bytes to new conversations only. Where the harness cannot do that, say in the report that in-flight conversations take one cold miss and, where the check is enforced, are rejected until their thinking blocks are dropped (next bullet).

"""
Neatlogs Anthropic wrapper.

Two usage patterns:

  1. Explicit wrap (primary):
     >>> import neatlogs, anthropic
     >>> client = neatlogs.wrap(anthropic.Anthropic())
     >>> client.messages.create(...)

  2. Import replacement (Langfuse-style):

"""Stagehand's lookup model as a bring-your-own-LLM callback on our neatlogs-wrapped Anthropic client.

Stagehand calls `generate` for every inference behind act, observe and extract
(see https://docs.stagehand.dev/v4/configuration/models.md, "Custom models").
Going through our own client makes each call a neatlogs LLM span with tokens,
cost and prompt, and lets us account for its cost ourselves.

Stagehand invokes the callback from a task its RPC reader starts, so the call
does not inherit the context of the tool that triggered it. Functions marked
with `@lookups_nest_here` (look and the do rungs) record their context, and
`generate` runs inside a copy of it: the LLM span then nests under that tool's
span, and `current_run` points at the run whose usage it adds to.
"""

import asyncio
import contextvars
import functools
import json
import re

import neatlogs
from anthropic import AsyncAnthropic
from stagehand import LLMStructuredGenerateResult

from config import LOOKUP_CALLBACK_MODEL, LOOKUP_MAX_TOKENS

_client = None
# The context of the innermost running `@lookups_nest_here` function. One
# Stagehand session runs at a time per worker process, so one slot is enough.
_caller_context: contextvars.Context | None = None


def _anthropic():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = neatlogs.wrap(AsyncAnthropic())
    return _client


def lookups_nest_here(function):
    """Make Stagehand model calls made while `function` runs nest under its span.

    Place it below the `@neatlogs.span` decorator so the recorded context includes that span.
    """

    @functools.wraps(function)
    async def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        global _caller_context
        previous, _caller_context = _caller_context, contextvars.copy_context()
        try:
            return await function(*args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            _caller_context = previous

    return wrapper


async def generate(params) -> LLMStructuredGenerateResult:
    """The callback passed to Stagehand.create as `model`."""
    if _caller_context is None:
        return await _generate(params)
    # A copy per call, because a Context can be entered by only one task at a time.
    return await asyncio.create_task(_generate(params), context=_caller_context.copy())


async def _generate(params) -> LLMStructuredGenerateResult:
    response_format = getattr(params, "response_format", None)
    if getattr(response_format, "type", None) != "json_schema":
        raise TypeError("Stagehand only issues structured generations")

    schema = response_format.schema_.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    schema.pop("$schema", None)
    # A tool's input must be an object; wrap any other schema and unwrap the answer.
    wrapped = schema.get("type") != "object"
    input_schema = (
        {"type": "object", "properties": {"value": schema}, "required": ["value"]} if wrapped else schema
    )
    tool_name = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]", "_", response_format.name)[:64] or "respond"
    tool = {
        "name": tool_name,
        "description": response_format.description or "Return the requested result.",
        "input_schema": input_schema,
    }

    request = {
        "model": LOOKUP_CALLBACK_MODEL,
        "max_tokens": LOOKUP_MAX_TOKENS,
        "messages": [
            {"role": message.role.value, "content": _content(message.content)} for message in params.messages
        ],
        "tools": [tool],
        # Forcing the one tool makes the answer arrive as tool input that follows the schema.
        "tool_choice": {"type": "tool", "name": tool_name},
    }
    # Stagehand's temperature is dropped: Claude Haiku 5.5 rejects non-default sampling parameters.
    if params.system_prompt:
        request["system"] = [
            {"type": "text", "text": params.system_prompt, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}
        ]

    response = await _anthropic().messages.create(**request)
    _account(response)

    tool_use = next((block for block in response.content if block.type == "tool_use"), None)
    if tool_use is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Lookup model returned no tool call (stop_reason={response.stop_reason})")
    structured = tool_use.input["value"] if wrapped else tool_use.input

    usage = response.usage
    cache_read = usage.cache_read_input_tokens or 0
    input_tokens = usage.input_tokens + (usage.cache_creation_input_tokens or 0) + cache_read
    return LLMStructuredGenerateResult.model_validate({
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": {"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(structured)},
        "stop_reason": response.stop_reason,
        "output_format": "json_schema",
        "structured_content": structured,
        # Stagehand counts cached tokens inside input tokens; Anthropic reports them separately.
        "usage": {
            "input_tokens": input_tokens,
            "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens,
            "total_tokens": input_tokens + usage.output_tokens,
            "cached_input_tokens": cache_read,
        },
    })


def _content(content) -> list[dict]:
    blocks = content if isinstance(content, list) else [content]
    return [_block(block.root) for block in blocks]


def _block(block) -> dict:
    if block.type == "text":
        return {"type": "text", "text": block.text}
    if block.type == "image":
        return {"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": block.mime_type, "data": block.data}}
    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported content block for the lookup model: {block.type}")


def _account(response) -> None:
    # Imported here to avoid a cycle: tools imports this module.
    from tools import current_run

    ctx = current_run.get(None)
    if ctx is not None:
        ctx.usage.add_lookup_response(response)

Usage: python run_once.py --url URL --goal "GOAL"

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv(Path(__file__).parent / ".env")

neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], workflow_name="first-visit-test")

from config import BRAIN_EFFORT, BRAIN_MODEL  # noqa: E402
from visit import first_visit  # noqa: E402


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run one first-time visitor against a web app.")
    parser.add_argument("--url", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--goal", required=True)
